issues.description: The problem specification (UML) defines Stock.take(String) to return an int, and the reference solution implements take(String) returning an int. However, the template's Stock.take(String) returns a boolean. This discrepancy will cause compilation errors and confusion for students implementing SealSaloon methods that call stock.take(...) and expect an int (for example checking for -1), preventing them from following the intended design.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template implementation of Stock.take(String) to return an int with the same semantics as shown in the solution: return -1 when the ingredient is missing or quantity < 1, otherwise decrement quantity and return the new quantity. This will align the template with the problem specification and the reference solution.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML declares Stock.take(String): int (and Stock.add(String): int) while the provided template's Stock.take method returns boolean. The solution implements Stock.take(String): int and uses the -1 return value to signal failure. This mismatch in the method contract (return type/semantics for take) across problem statement, template, and solution creates a mapping/confusion for students: they may read the specification/UML expecting an int-based contract but find a boolean implementation in the template and be unsure which behavior to follow when implementing SealSaloon methods that call stock.take(...).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Stock.take method signature and semantics consistent across artifacts. Either update the template Stock.take to return int and use -1 to indicate failure (matching the UML/problem statement and the solution), or modify the problem statement and solution to use a boolean-returning take consistently. Prefer updating the template to Stock.take(String): int with the same semantics as the solution.
